said.text: Build the project manager so everything can be its own project, its own instance of the console. A setting to enable multi-project view, the entire console appears in that group with each project's console running. A project type: one for development of itself or framework tools like the console, one for creating new apps using all the tools in the console. The new app will actively render in a preview window, a floating or dockable section.

# Build: project-manager-every-project-its-own-console-in

At: 2026-11-10T15:40:27.752Z

A setting to enable multi-project view, the entire console appears in that group with each project's console running. A project type: one for development of itself or framework tools like the console, one for creating new apps using all the tools in the console. ## What to build
Continue build "Project Manager: every project its own console instance, multi-project tab view, project types (self/framework dev vs new app), live app preview window" (project-manager-every-project-its-own-console-in) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-10 15:40):
"Build the project manager so everything can be its own project, its own instance of the console. A setting to enable multi-project view, the entire console appears in that group with each project's console running. A project type: one for development of itself or framework tools like the console, one for creating new apps using all the tools in the console. The new app will actively render in a preview window, a floating or dockable section."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~1.3 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) Builds on the create/move-projects build. 1) Project Manager plugin: create, open, rename and switch projects; each project is its own instance of the console with its own builds, notes, data. 2) Setting: Multi-project view. When on, the console shows a group (tab group) with each project's console running side by side. 3) Project type: (a) Framework/self development: developing the console itself or framework tools (the console builds itself); (b) New app: uses all the console's tools to generate a new, real app. 4) Live preview: the app being built renders live in a separate floating or dockable preview window while you work in the console. Full API control, no AI needed.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) Build the project manager so everything can be its own project, its own instance of the console. A setting to enable multi-project view, the entire console appears in that group with each project's console running. A project type: one for development of itself or framework tools like the console, one for creating new apps using all the tools in the console. The new app will actively render in a preview window, a floating or dockable section.
[ ] s3 (~20 min) Tests green, report _claude/builds/reports/project-manager-every-project-its-own-console-in.md, THREADS row, commit, push, PR
Read first: _claude/builds/reports/project-manager-every-project-its-own-console-in.md, _claude/THREADS.md
Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step project-manager-every-project-its-own-console-in <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link project-manager-every-project-its-own-console-in --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.
